memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua told the people, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will do amazing things among you." — Josh 3:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the miracle came the call: "Consecrate yourselves." To consecrate means to set apart, to prepare oneself for God, to clear away anything unclean and get ready for His holy work. Joshua is telling the people, in effect, "God is about to do something wonderful, so prepare your hearts."

There is a beautiful order here. Preparation comes before the powerful work of God. The Israelites could not make the river part — only God could do that. Yet God called them to ready themselves first. We cannot manufacture God's blessing, but we can prepare our hearts to receive it. A clean, expectant heart is fertile ground for what God wants to do.

And what a promise: "tomorrow the Lord will do amazing things among you." God does the amazing things; the people simply position themselves in readiness and expectation. Notice too that God gave them advance notice, building faith and anticipation. He often stirs our expectancy before He acts.

For us, consecration is a daily reality in Christ. We set ourselves apart for God, confessing sin and yielding our hearts, not to earn His work but to be ready for it. As we offer ourselves as "living sacrifices" (Rom 12:1), we position ourselves to see what God will do. He still delights to do amazing things among a people prepared to receive them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What might God be asking you to clear away as you consecrate yourself to Him?
2. Are you living with expectation that God can still do "amazing things"?
3. How does daily yielding to God prepare you to receive His work?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I set myself apart for You today. Cleanse my heart and make me ready, for I believe You still do amazing things among Your people. Amen.
